assessment.summary: ABL1 is one of the most extensively validated and successfully drugged kinase targets in oncology, with 7 approved drugs including imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib, and bosutinib, primarily for BCR-ABL1-driven chronic myeloid leukemia. Structural characterization is exceptional, with 85 PDB entries at resolutions as low as 1.03Å and the majority of top structures bearing bound ligands. Chemical and literature evidence is among the strongest available for any human kinase target.
evidence_gaps: AlphaFold mean pLDDT of 63.4 is relatively low, reflecting disordered regions (e.g., N-terminal SH3/SH2 linkers, activation loop flexibility), but this is not a concern given the wealth of experimental PDB structures
Resistance mutations (e.g., T315I gatekeeper) remain a clinical challenge; coverage of all clinically relevant mutant structures may be incomplete
Allosteric binding sites beyond the ATP pocket are less chemically characterized despite structural knowledge of myristoyl pocket
Emerging non-CML indications (e.g., CHDSKM syndrome from germline gain-of-function variants) are less clinically validated and may require different therapeutic strategies
Selectivity profiles across the full kinome for newer-generation inhibitors may not be fully captured in ChEMBL entries
